newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-ING still on prowl after U.S. insurance buy.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-ING still on prowl after U.S. insurance buy.

text.p: Dutch financial services group ING Groep NV dipped into its huge financial war chest on Tuesday, agreeing a $2.2 billion bid for U.S. life insurer Equitable of Iowa Companies.

Although the $68 per share deal was its largest takeover to date, the Dutch banking and insurance group said its appetite for expansion remained and it reaffirmed plans to expand further in the United States and Europe.
The takeover, long anticipated by the market in view of the group's growing cash mountain estimated at up to $5 billion, was applauded by analysts and shares in ING surged to a record high.
"In terms of product mix, distribution channels and geographic spread, Equitable of Iowa complements ING's existing life insurance business in an excellent way," ING said.

The deal, set to take effect in the fourth quarter pending shareholder and regulatory approval, is ING's biggest acquisition since the group was formed through a merger of NMB Postbank with insurer Nationale Nederlanden in 1991.
ING said it planned to pay up to 60 percent of the purchase sum in ING shares it already held. The rest would be paid in borrowed funds.
Executive chairman Aad Jacobs said ING's ambition to be one of the top 10 players in U.S. life insurance had not been satisfied by the acquisition, taking it only into the top 20.

Jacobs also said the Dutch banking and insurance group was working hard to expand in corporate banking in Europe, particularly in Germany and France, and it still intended to buy a U.S. investment bank.
"We are a very rich company and we can afford to make a number of steps forward," he said in a telephone interview, adding that acquisitions must enhance earnings per share (EPS).
The acquisition would boost EPS by about one percent in the first year and roughly double ING's U.S. life insurance premium income to $4.3 billion, he said.

ING spokesman Ruud Polet told Reuters that ING's North American life insurance operations were active in the higher and lower income segments of the life insurance market while the U.S. company was strong in the middle segment. "It's a perfect fit in terms of segment," he said.

ING, which had long indicated its interest in making a U.S. life insurance acquisition, had been looking specifically at Equitable of Iowa for a couple of months, he said. The acquisition has the backing of the Equitable of Iowa board.
Investors on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange cheered the news, sending ING shares 7.60 guilders higher to 103.20 after which they settled at 102.10 around 1125 GMT.
Analysts were also upbeat on the deal, although some said it was expensive.
"It's a good strategic move, notably because it will increase the stability of ING's earnings, since the proportion of life insurance gets bigger," said Bart van der Feen, banking analyst with IRIS.
"The deal looks positive," agreed Delta Lloyd Bank's Dennis Ederzeel. "But you can argue that the price is high. ING is paying 17 times next year's profit for Iowa."
But he added ING could afford paying a premium in view of its own high price/earnings ratio of close on 21 times earnings.
